items.title: Jimmy Heath interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, September 8, 2014
items.q: Just like I was listening to Glenn Miller on the TV last night. Because I heard that when I was a kid.

ctx.x: I played the record once and I was done with it. And even Mingus, I heard he said the same thing, it sounded like everybody in the practice room warming up to go on the stage. There’s no distinctive melody there. And what is music? Now we’ve got music that is words and a rhythm and no melody and no harmony. And that is not music to me. It’s music by the kids. They think it’s music. Every generation has their time. My brother went to his death, Percy, told me, “Aww that ain’t gonna last.” I say, “Yes it is Percy.”…

items.title: Jimmy Heath — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Who’s that? Tommy Dorsey, Glen Millis.

ctx.x: Well, hearing you talk about Youtube, and all of the things that can pull up, all of these archival performances from people; do you spend a lot of time just listening casually to music? Do you listen to music at home?

Yeah. I’ve been stuck this year listening to Delius, Frederick Delius. He’s like, for lack of another word, I like romantic, I like melodic. The romantic era: Debussey, and Ravel, he’s in that bag, Frederick Delius. I’ve been listening, in retrospect, to, I’ve got some recordings by a company called Chronolgical Classics from France. I’ve got five C.D.’s of Jimmy Lunceford’s band. I haven’t talked to Wynton since we did the thing with Willie Nelson, with Cosby. I have to tell him he’s been doing everybody but…

it when I was a kid. I heard all the big bands, I heard Tommy Dorsey when “I’ll never smile again” (Imitates Dorsey). All that, you know when Frankie was there. Being around the giants of music, and I told a lot of these stories that are going to be in this documentation, in my book. I told about Coltrane and I, with Dizzy and we’d go to the Riverside Theatre in Milwaukee. We were opening the next day, so we both loved Jimmy Dorsey’s alto saxophone playing because we were both playing altos, at the time, in…
